memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If one of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will be unclean, and you must break the pot." - Lev 11:33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Wood could be washed. Cloth could be soaked. But a clay pot had to be broken.

The reason is simple: unglazed clay is porous. It absorbs. Whatever soaked into it could not be rinsed out again. There was no washing this one clean, so it had to go.

Sometimes God asks us to break the pot. Not to clean up a habit but to end it. Not to manage a relationship that is pulling us away from Christ but to walk away from it. Not to limit the time we spend somewhere, but to stop going. Jesus spoke in strong language about cutting off what causes us to stumble (Matt 5:29-30) — not because our bodies are evil, but because some things cannot be negotiated with. They can only be broken.

We resist this. We prefer washing to breaking. Breaking costs something, and it is public, and it is final.

But notice what the broken pot protects: the holiness of a household that belongs to God. There is something so valuable at stake that a pot is worth losing.

Paul says we hold this treasure in jars of clay, to show that the surpassing power belongs to God (2 Cor 4:7). Sometimes the clay must break — and even then, God is not finished with us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something in your life God is asking you to break rather than manage?
2. What has stopped you from making that decisive break so far?
3. What is the treasure you are protecting by doing so?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me courage where I have been settling for half measures. If something must be broken and not merely managed, give me the honesty to see it and the strength to do it. Amen.
